There was a time when the future of folding smartphones—whether flip-style or book-style—was uncertain, but for now at least, the book-style design is clearly the winner.

Samsung's eighth-generation foldable phone adopts this design, and the upcoming iPhone Ultra is expected to do the same, as are the leaked images of the Xiaomi 18 Fold…

Foldable smartphones generally come in two form factors, commonly known as flip-style and book-style.

The flip-style design essentially folds a regular smartphone in half, making the body thicker but halving its height, delivering a standard-sized screen in a more portable package. The Motorola Razr is one example, its design inspiration actually traces back to Motorola's classic model that pioneered this approach back in 2004.

The book-style design's name is self-explanatory: a device closer to a square shape unfolds into a small tablet, similar to an iPad mini. This is the design Apple is expected to unveil next month.

Samsung's Galaxy Z Fold series has popularised this design, having just launched its eighth-generation model last month.

Now Xiaomi is also preparing to join the fray with their 18 Fold. The camera module design of this phone bears considerable resemblance to the expected iPhone Ultra styling. Weibo user Peter shared two photos (above), which he believes are of an engineering test unit rather than a final production version.

Our sister site 9to5Google notes that this deep cherry colour appears to reference one of the rumoured colours for the iPhone 18 Pro.
